You can hire an agent, sell without one, or accept a cash offer, and your timeline for getting paid should drive that choice. Still, the house's condition and a clean title shape how fast you finish more than the route does. A rough roof or an unclear deed slows every kind of buyer.

  • Pull the parcel number and tax bill from the Mohave County Treasurer before you talk to buyers.
  • Settle in advance whether to fix things, give the buyer a credit, or sell as-is.
  • Have every buyer put a closing date and the seller's costs on paper.

Bullhead City sits on the Arizona side of the Colorado River in western Mohave County, directly across from Laughlin, Nevada. The population estimate for July 1, 2025 is 43,987, up from 41,348 in April 2020. Owners live in 69.9 percent of the homes.

Bills come from the Mohave County Treasurer and are mailed by the first of October. October 1 is the due date, and most property can be paid in two installments. Installment one is past due after 5 pm on November 1. Installment two comes due March 1 and is past due after 5 pm on May 1. A bill of $100 or less is due in a single payment on October 1 and is past due after December 31. If you pay both installments by December 31, interest that built up after November 1 is removed. Should a deadline fall on a weekend or holiday, you have until 5 pm the next business day.

Paying late brings a 16 percent annual penalty, prorated monthly. Nothing obliges the Treasurer to mail a bill, so taxes are owed even when none arrives. A bill that arrives after you've sold should go to the buyer, or back to the Treasurer at P.O. Box 712, Kingman, AZ 86402, with the new owner's name written on it. Locally, a payment drop box is at 1130 Hancock Road in Bullhead City. Only the main office in Kingman takes cash.

Property tax relief is handled by the Mohave County Assessor, whose office runs exemptions for widows, widowers, disabled civilians and disabled former service members. For tax year 2026, the total allowable exemption was $4,873 of assessed limited property value, combined Arizona property could not exceed $36,454 in assessed value, and qualifying income could not exceed $39,865 per household, or $47,826 with minor children at home. The filing season starts in January and ends at the close of February.

State Aid to Education also reduces the primary school tax on owner-occupied homes. A mobile home that isn't affixed to the land can generate two tax notices, one for the land and one for the home, so a buyer of a mobile home should ask the Assessor whether it has been affixed. Qualifying depends on the buyer's own situation, and the Assessor decides. If you plan to hand the house to a buyer who may qualify, point them to the Assessor early so the paperwork can start once the deed is recorded.

The tax roll shows a new owner only after the deed is recorded with the Mohave County Recorder, which sends the information on to the Assessor. Most documents cost $30 to record, certification costs $3 and copies cost $1 per page. Make checks payable to the Mohave County Recorder. The transfer needs an Affidavit of Property Value under state rules, unless the deed bears an A.R.S. 11-1134 exemption code. Use the contract date as the date of sale.

For permits, ask Bullhead City's building and zoning staff whether work done on your house was permitted. Planning repairs before you list? Ask the city which jobs need a permit before any contractor begins.

  • Seller: deed, affidavit or exemption code, and the parcel number.
  • Recorder: collects the $30 recording fee.
  • Assessor: changes the owner name and mailing address once the deed is recorded.

A cash sale tends to run in this order. First, gather the deed, parcel number and latest tax bill. Second, choose between repairing, crediting the buyer or selling as-is, and get closing dates and seller costs in writing from each buyer. Third, once you sign, the title company totals the tax balance, drafts the deed and Affidavit of Property Value, and files them with the Mohave County Recorder. A cash buyer needs no lender, so no loan-approval wait ever begins.

Once the deed is on record, the Recorder passes the details to the Assessor, who updates the owner name and mailing address. Until that happens, bills for the house you sold may still reach you. Send them on to the new owner.

This choice affects both price and speed, so make it before you collect offers. Repairing before listing can raise what a buyer pays but costs money and time up front. A credit lets the buyer handle the work, and it shows up as a line on the closing statement. Selling as-is is simplest, and it is the choice cash buyers are most used to, though the price will reflect whatever an inspection finds.

Whichever you choose, confirm permits first. A buyer's inspector may ask for the permit record on finished work. Bullhead City building and zoning staff can tell you what applies to your address.

Two tax notices, one for the land and one for the home, can result when a mobile home isn't affixed to the land. Selling one means asking the Assessor whether yours has been affixed, then telling the buyer the answer. Call the Treasurer for the balance on each notice, and give both figures to the title company.

sections.h2: Before you list: a short tax check
sections.html: Spend ten minutes with the Treasurer's records before you talk price. Note whether the first installment has been paid and whether the second is still open. Look for anything older than the current year. Confirm the mailing address on the bill is the one you want used until closing. Then call the Treasurer if any line looks wrong, since a balance found at the closing table costs more time than one found today. A buyer paying cash can close quickly only if the tax figure is settled, so this small step protects the speed you were after in the first place.

faqs.q: When are Mohave County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Taxes are due October 1. The first installment is past due after 5 pm on November 1, and the second is due March 1 and past due after May 1. Taxes of $100 or less are past due after December 31.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Bullhead City?
faqs.a: The median value of an owner-occupied home is $211,500 for 2020 to 2024, and median gross rent is $1,079.

faqs.q: Where do I send a tax bill for a house I already sold?
faqs.a: Forward it to the new owner, or return it to the Mohave County Treasurer at P.O. Box 712, Kingman, AZ 86402 with the owner's name and date of sale.

faqs.q: How much does Mohave County charge to record a deed?
faqs.a: The Recorder charges $30 for most documents. Copies are $1 per page and certified copies add $3 per document.

faqs.q: When can I apply for a Mohave County property tax exemption?
faqs.a: Applications for widows, widowers, disabled civilians and disabled former service members open in January and close at the end of February. The Assessor decides who qualifies.
